author: CNN
description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s senior adviser for religious issues has shared scores of racist and homophobic posts, spread conspiracy theories, and repeatedly denigrated Islam and immigrants, a CNN investigation has found. Ryan Higgins has become a key aide to Hegseth since joining the Pentagon, multiple sources familiar with the matter told CNN, particularly in shaping the defense secretary’s embrace of Christian nationalist themes in speeches and public appearances.

On his social media platforms, CNN found Higgins defended a video President Donald Trump shared depicting the Obamas as apes, said same-sex marriage was “abominable,” and speculated about how many abortions former Vice President Kamala Harris might have had, citing her age and claiming she had a “long record of sleeping around.”

CNN senior investigative reporter Allison Gordon shares her reporting and Rep. Adam Smith of the Armed Services Committee reacts to Higgins' posts.

0:00 CNN uncovers Higgins' racist and hom
title: 'Separation of church & state doesn't exist' says Hegseth faith adviser

author: CNN
description:
Alex Pretti's parents demanded answers Tuesday, saying the federal government has stayed silent for 275 days since immigration agents shot and killed their son, a US citizen, in Minneapolis in January. 

The day of the shooting, the Department of Homeland Security posted that agents were conducting a targeted operation when an “individual approached US Border Patrol officers with a 9 mm semi-automatic handgun” and that after they tried to "disarm the subject," an agent "fired defensive shots," though video of the incident disputed those claims. 

CNN has reached out to the DOJ and the US Attorney for Minnesota.
title: Alex Pretti's parents plead for justice 275 days after fatal ICE shooting

description:

Some are calling it a “creeping mobilization”. 

Also, Russia expert Jill Dougherty explains why the prospect of successful peace talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin remain "very questionable," while Trump's recent tilt towards Moscow is placing increased pressure on Ukraine.

description:
President Donald Trump shrugged off any concern about holding Mississippi’s Senate seat during a visit Monday, even as his very presence in the ruby-red state underscored persistent Republican concerns about once-safe seats. 

During his speech, he responded to former President Barack Obama, who lambasted Trump’s fixation on renovations over the weekend, likening it to Saddam Hussein opening a Cheesecake Factory. 

“He doesn’t understand,” Trump said of the former president. “The White House has to be clean, pristine, beautiful.” 

CNN's Michael Smerconish and his NewsNight panel discuss Trump's long-running feud with Obama and Erin Burnett's panel reacts to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's visit to a Cheesecake Factory.
